source.title: Scaling of Capability and Efficiency at Inference Time in Large Reasoning Models
source.authors: Moritz Laber; Zohair Shafi; Germans Savcisens; Brennan Klein; Matteo Chinazzi; Samuel V. Scarpino; A. Barabási; Alessandro Vespignani; Tina Eliassi-Rad

record.file_problem: none; full paper and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether model performance on reasoning tasks scales predictably with model size, using task-correctness data and a capability-scale model rather than held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses classical pretraining loss scaling and cites the original sources, but does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit loss laws, extrapolate loss, test compute-optimal parameter/token allocations, or compare architectures at fixed parameter count. Its inference-time reasoning results are not results on those measures.
record.test_reason: The study measures how correctness on four synthetic reasoning tasks changes with parameter count (1.5B–70B) in DeepSeek-R1-Distill models. It fits the characteristic solvable instance size as a power law in N. That is a direct result on V6 (downstream performance vs scale) in a new setting: distilled reasoning models at inference time. T3 fits better than T2 because the scale series is a distilled family on different Qwen/Llama bases, not a controlled pretraining sweep, and the measure is not pretraining loss. No loss, allocation or architecture results exist for V1–V5 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that larger DeepSeek-R1-Distill models solve larger instances, with the characteristic solvable size growing sublinearly in N (diminishing returns). Output-length efficiency shows weak or no improvement with size. They argue this questions naive scaling and flag generalization beyond this family and these tasks, and confounding from different distillation bases and tokenizers, as open.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates inference-time correctness and response length on generated reasoning problems, rather than measuring held-out pretraining loss or fitting the original pretraining scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Capability exponent estimates vary by task, temperature, and statistical model (FAM versus VAM); the preferred model also differs by task.

fits_no_version.finding: Output length of correct answers grows as a power law in instance size, with exponents 0.41–0.89. Its prefactor shows no systematic change with model size: e.g. index τ=0.6 PM β(A)=-0.03 [-0.32,0.25]. Brackets τ=0.4 shows a weak increase, β(A)=0.15 [0.00,0.29].
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token efficiency of correct reasoning outputs does not improve systematically with model size in distilled reasoning models.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed N, the probability of solving an instance decays roughly exponentially with instance size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-task accuracy declines exponentially with problem size at fixed model scale.

record.problems: The experiments cover one distilled model family and four generated reasoning tasks; generalization beyond them is explicitly unresolved. The capability results depend in part on task, temperature, and statistical model. The study reports model-level posterior means that can be non-monotonic in individual conditions.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant rows left out. The paper's output-length and efficiency results are summarized under fits_no_version rather than catalogued as separate rows because they do not measure any listed claim version.

untested.parts: No extrapolation of fitted laws to larger runs; all five sizes are fitted jointly.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed N.
No other modality or training regime for the loss power-law form. Inference-time reasoning performance is covered under V6 instead.
Predictability from pretraining loss. General downstream benchmarks. Extrapolation of the capability law beyond 70B.
No fitting-dependence analysis of pretraining loss exponents or compute-optimal splits.

missing.what: Per-model posterior ν values, showing non-monotonic capability across sizes in many conditions, including FAM fits (e.g. index FAM 14B 615 > 32B 287; brackets FAM 14B 390 > 32B 302)
elpd model comparison: VAM is preferred for brackets and parity at all temperatures, FAM for addition and index. This is needed to know which exponent is the better-supported estimate.
Random-effect deviations from the latent capability law: η(ν) 0.20–0.52, meaning sizeable scatter around the power law for non-addition tasks

record.verdict_notes: The parameter series spans different base models (Qwen 1.5B–32B, Llama 70B), so N is confounded with base model and tokenizer, as the authors note. Labels are split by statistical model because the elpd-preferred fit for brackets and parity gives much weaker exponents than FAM. The reader's reliance on CrI excluding zero hid that preference. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolating held-out loss from smaller pretraining runs to larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and how either quantity scales with training compute.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Whether the pretraining-loss power-law form transfers to other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests task correctness scaling with model size on synthetic reasoning problems, not general downstream benchmarks or predictability from pretraining loss.
Setup and fitting dependence of held-out loss exponents or compute-optimal splits.

relationships.condition: Addition (FAM and VAM, all temperatures), index (FAM and VAM, all temperatures), and brackets/parity under FAM
relationships.reason: The capability decay scale grows as a sublinear power of N with credible intervals above zero: β 0.51–0.75 under FAM, 0.42–0.61 for addition/index under VAM (r1–r15, r19–r21).
relationships.display_finding: Capability decay scales had positive sublinear size exponents of 0.51–0.75 under FAM and 0.42–0.61 for addition and index under VAM, with credible intervals above zero.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Addition (FAM and VAM, all temperatures), index (FAM and VAM, all temperatures), and brackets/parity under FAM
source_check.reason: All listed exponents have positive 95% credible intervals; their posterior means support increasing characteristic solvable size with parameter count.

relationships.condition: Brackets (τ 0.4, 0.8) and parity (all τ) under VAM, which elpd prefers for these tasks
relationships.reason: Under the better-fitting model, exponents fall to 0.25–0.34 with intervals reaching or crossing zero, and per-model ν is non-monotonic. Predictable scaling of these tasks depends on the statistical-model choice (r16, r18, r22–r24).
relationships.display_finding: The preferred VAM fit yielded exponents of 0.25–0.34 with intervals reaching or crossing zero, while per-model ν varied nonmonotonically.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Brackets (τ 0.4, 0.8) and parity (all τ) under VAM, which elpd prefers for these tasks
source_check.reason: The preferred VAM yields weaker scaling than FAM, with plateaus or non-monotonic model-specific estimates. Correct the rationale: brackets τ=0.4 has CrI [0.06,0.46] and parity τ=0.4 has [0.01,0.67], both strictly positive; only the other listed intervals reach or cross zero. Brackets τ=0.4 is monotonic.

relationships.condition: Brackets task, τ=0.6 (recommended temperature), VAM (preferred by elpd)
relationships.reason: β=0.07 [-0.17,0.30], and ν stays near 27–45 from 1.5B to 70B, so there is no capability scaling in this fit (r17).
relationships.display_finding: The fit gave β=0.07 with interval [−0.17, 0.30], while ν stayed near 27–45 across 1.5B to 70B, indicating no clear capability gain.

source_check.reason: Table A1 gives β=0.07 [-0.17,0.30]; Table A2 gives characteristic scales 27,42,39,45,34 across increasing model sizes. These show no clear capability improvement in this condition, although uncertainty does not establish an exactly zero effect.

relation.reason: Measures correctness across model sizes and estimates capability-scaling exponents, directly bearing on V6.

tranche.reason: Tests downstream capability versus parameter count in a new setting: distilled reasoning models evaluated on four synthetic tasks.

source_check.notes: The authors interpret all posterior means as sublinear capability scaling; the absent/partial distinctions are the catalog's interpretation of uncertainty and model-specific estimates. Generalization is limited by one distilled family, four tasks, and differing base models/tokenizers.

reader_labels.reason: The fitted characteristic instance-size scale rises with model size in these conditions; see r1-r16, r19-r22.
